item.title: Game Thread: Michigan Football at Rutgers
item.description: Michigan Football returns to action Saturday afternoon, traveling to Piscataway for a Halloween matchup against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights. With both teams struggling to find consistency this season, the Wolverines will look to reel things in and build some much-needed momentum heading into November. Michigan enters Saturday’s contest with a 4-3 record (1-3 Big Ten) after suffering a frustrating 13-6 loss to Indiana last weekend. Despite holding the sixth-ranked Hoosiers to just 212 total yards, the Wolverines failed to find the end zone, continuing a troubling stretch of offensive performances. Freshman quarterback Tommy Carr struggled in his first career start, completing 20-of-32 passes for 167 yards and an interception. Michigan’s rushing attack also failed to establish itself, finishing with just 57 net yards on the ground. Fortunately for the Wolverines, Saturday presents an opportunity to get things moving in the right direction against a Rutgers defense that has struggled mightily this season. The Scarlet Knights enter at 2-5 overall (1-3 Big Ten), having lost three of their last four games. Rutgers has been particularly bad defensively, allowing approximately seven yards per play while ranking near the bottom of the country in several categories. Michigan’s offense will also have an opportunity to capitalize on a Rutgers team that has struggled to protect the football. The Scarlet Knights have averaged more than two turnovers per game, including 11 interceptions through seven contests. Rutgers is also dealing with significant personnel concerns, as quarterback Dylan Lonergan has been ruled out, while standout wide receiver KJ Duff — who has recorded 774 receiving yards and nine touchdowns this season — is listed as questionable. However, the Wolverines have their own injury concerns to navigate, as offensive lineman Blake Frazier, defensive linemen Enow Etta, John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols, and safeties Rod Moore Jr. and Jordan Young were questionable on Friday’s availability report. With Michigan needing two more victories to secure bowl eligibility, this matchup presents an opportunity the Wolverines can ill afford to squander. item.title: 5 Things I Think I Think About the Miami Dolphins After Week 7
item.description: Wait, what? Did the Miami Dolphins respond to arguably their worst loss of the season with their first win? On the road? You bet your sweet bippy they did. And against the Jets too – if you tell me the Dolphins go 2-15 this season but sweep the Jets, I’d say, “You know, not so bad.” Here are five more things I think I think following the Dolphins’ first win. They Did the One Thing Winning Teams Do If there’s one ultimate flex in professional football, it’s this: Running the ball to drain the clock and close out a close game. Everybody in the stadium knows exactly what’s coming: The defense knows, the crowd knows, the broadcast team knows, everybody knows. And it doesn’t matter – the winning team lines up and closes the game anyway. On Sunday, that’s unexpectedly what the Dolphins were able to do against the Jets. Late in the fourth quarter, the Jets scored a touchdown (Mason Taylor?! Again?!) to pull within three points. They then kicked off, hoping to force a stop and get the ball back to tie or win it. The old Dolphins would have played conservative, forcing the Jets to burn their timeouts but giving Gang Green the ball and a chance to win. But what did the new Dolphins do? 3:17 left, 1 st down, 14-yard run from Ollie Gordon. Jets timeout. 3:10 left, 1 st down, 7-yard run from Ollie Gordon. Jets timeout. 3:04 left, 2 nd down, 1-yard run from Ollie Gordon. 2:21 left, 3 rd down, 1-yard run from Ollie Gordon. Two-minute warning. 2:00 left, 4 th down, 2-yard run from Malik Willis. First down. Victory formation. I mean, it wasn’t pure dominance: They needed a two-yard pickup on fourth down to secure the win, whereas ideally you’d lock that in on second or third down. Still, if you want to talk about the growth of a young team, this is Exhibit A with a gold star. Malik Willis Showed Tangible Growth What a difference a bye week makes, eh? Let’s revel in the stat line: 14-of-21 passing 228 passing yards 2 passing touchdowns 0 interceptions, 0 fumbles 37 rushing yards 1 rushing touchdown QB rating of 130.7! So what caused the change? A good night’s sleep? Frank Thomas’ testosterone supplements?* Yes and yes. But also, maybe better decision-making and resource utilization. Instead of going for deep shot after deep shot, against the Jets Willis threw more passes that were short of the sticks, completing a season-high 67% of his passes and keeping the offense on schedule. He also involved his tight ends more, with TE Greg Dulcich leading the team in targets and a season-high 86 yards, and he clearly benefited from having No. 1 receiver Caleb Douglas back. Willis still has more questions than answers right now, of course. But after opening the season with just two touchdown passes against seven turnovers, Sunday felt like the first game that provided a legitimate reason for optimism. item.title: World record at 40! Sikandar Raza smashes unbeaten ton against Afghanistan, enters elite list
item.description: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza created history with a stunning unbeaten century against Afghanistan in the second T20I in Sharjah on Thursday. The 40-year-old scored 106 not out off just 56 balls, hitting five fours and nine sixes. However, his brilliant effort could not prevent Zimbabwe from losing by 19 runs as Afghanistan secured an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Raza became the first Zimbabwean batter to score two centuries in T20 internationals. He also made history as the oldest batter from a Full Member nation to score a T20I century, achieving the feat at 40 years and 188 days. Germany's Mussadiq Ahmed remains the first player overall to score a T20I hundred at the age of 40, having made 122 against Austria earlier this year. He joined debutant Tafadzwa Tsiga, and the pair put together an unbeaten 120-run partnership for the sixth wicket. Tsiga contributed 31 not out from 23 balls, but Zimbabwe could only manage 202 for five, falling short of the target. Afghanistan recover from early collapse Earlier, Zimbabwe's bowlers had put Afghanistan under serious pressure after reducing them to 38 for five. Brad Evans struck twice in the opening over, dismissing Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Mohammad Akram. Kundai Matigimu then removed Ibrahim Zadran and Shahidullah with his first two deliveries. Their attacking batting helped Afghanistan reach 221 for seven, scoring 176 runs in the final 10 overs. Meanwhile, Rashid Khan made history of his own by becoming the first bowler in men's T20I cricket to take 200 wickets.

item.title: Everton striker's relief family not home during burglary
item.description: Thierno Barry scored Everton's third goal in their Carabao Cup fourth round match [Press Association] Everton striker Thierno Barry has said he was relieved that his family were not at home when it was burgled while he played in a cup match. His home in Greater Manchester was targeted while he was playing for Everton against Newcastle United in a Carabao Cup tie at the Hill Dickinson stadium on Thursday. The Frenchman, 24, posted on Instagram "things could have been much worse" had his partner and toddler not been in the stands. A spokesman for Greater Manchester Police said an investigation was ongoing. Barry posted that he would not put his family "at risk" in the future by posting about his life on social media. He said: "Maybe I've been too open about my family's life and mine, potentially putting them at risk, all just to show my lifestyle and inspire others through my journey and success, hoping to motivate them to do the same. "My childhood was never easy, but I've always believed that when you give yourself the best possible chances, there is always hope. "Unfortunately, in life, there are people and things beyond our control." 'People you love' The father-of-one added: "This has been a lesson for me. "The most important thing in life is to look after and protect the people you love. "That's what truly matters. Everything else is just materialistic." A GMP spokeswoman said that "officers are currently investigating reports of a burglary on Thursday evening" at "an address in the Bowdon area of Trafford". She added: "No arrests have been made at this stage, and enquiries are ongoing." Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to progress to the fifth round, with Barry scoring the winning goal. item.title: Tarik Skubal Predicted To Join NL Central Club Over Other Contenders
item.description: Free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline, and after failing to win the World Series after their all-in move, they must now decide if they want to retain him as a free agent. Skubal is a two-time American League Cy Young Award winner and was great again this year for the Detroit Tigers and the Dodgers. Any team would love to have him, but his price tag will limit which teams actually have a chance to get him. The real contenders are all big-market teams, and SNY's John Harper predicted he would sign with the Chicago Cubs. The Cubs would seem like one of the least likely big markets to land Skubal, especially if the Dodgers, New York Mets and New York Yankees make an effort. However, they are desperate for an ace and have a ton of money coming off the books. "After a quick exit in the postseason, the Cubs have more than $100 million coming off their payroll, a glaring need for an ace, and the added incentive of knowing their neighbors to the north, the rival Brewers, just won the World Series," wrote Harper. "All of which I believe will add up to them outbidding the Mets, the Dodgers, and anybody else who pursues Skubal, even if it means going to eight years at $45 million or so per season." Skubal would not fix the Cubs' rotation single-handedly, but he would go a long way in doing so. He is a true ace, and the Cubs would have a great chance to win the 30-plus games he starts a season. However, they would still need to fill the spots behind him. Edward Cabrera struggled and dealt with injuries last year and Cade Horton could be out for the year. item.title: Why Colts are playing Jonathan Taylor in Week 8 despite trade rumors heating up
item.description: Why Colts are playing Jonathan Taylor in Week 8 despite trade rumors heating up originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jonathan Taylor trade rumors are picking up a lot of steam heading into the Indianapolis Colts ' Week 8 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars . Saturday morning revealed that the Colts are seemingly more open to a trade with Taylor than before, and it looks like a trade is very much on the table for Indianapolis. So, with the odds of a deal increasing, will Taylor even play in Week 8? According to ESPN's Stephen Holder , Taylor is still set to play for the Colts on Sunday. So, with that in mind, why are the Colts, despite the trade rumors picking up a lot of steam lately, not benching Taylor? Why Jonathan Taylor is still set to play for Colts despite trade rumors heating up "As of now, Jonathan Taylor IS playing tomorrow," Holder reports. "No deal is imminent, and I imagine they want to send the message that they are willing to keep him (which I do believe is true)." So, while conventional wisdom might suggest that the Colts should bench Taylor and protect him from getting hurt and ruining his trade value, the Colts still plan to play the star running back on Sunday. One of the reasons, as Holder notes, is to prove to other teams around the NFL that they're willing to keep Taylor. Benching him would prove that they fully intend to trade him away. The Colts wouldn't bench a star player like Taylor if a trade weren't already completed or agreed upon. If Taylor doesn't play, the Colts tip their hand and would effectively ruin the leverage they have in trade talks. MORE : NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts ’ Jonathan Taylor Benching Taylor without having a trade in place would be a mistake. Besides, there's still a decent chance Taylor won't be traded, even as these rumors heat up Saturday morning. If they benched him but ended up keeping him, their decision to sit him in Week 8 would look a lot stranger than if they play him in Week 8 and then trade him the following week. At the end of the day, the Colts are planning to play Taylor in Week 8 against the AFC South rival Jaguars, despite trade rumors picking up a lot of steam about the star RB. They are running the risk of injury with Taylor, but they can limit his reps in this game to preserve his health, while still giving him a chance to see the field for what could be the final time with the Colts. This Colts team is selling, as they've already shipped out Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and Josh Downs has requested a trade. Taylor might be on the move, and that could still be the case even if he plays on Sunday. item.title: Brazil wrap up preparations for China in U-17 World Cup quarter-finals
item.description: Brazil wrap up preparations for China in U-17 World Cup quarter-finals Brazil’s U-17 Women’s National Team wrapped up preparations on Saturday morning (31) for their quarter-final clash against China at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. The match will take place this Sunday (1) at 3 p.m. (Brasília time) at the Mohammed VI Women’s Football Complex in Morocco. In their final session before the decisive clash, head coach Rilany Silva led the team through intensive movement and positioning drills, focusing on tactical adjustments for the match. The coaching staff also paid special attention to set pieces and penalties, preparing the squad for different scenarios and situations that could arise during the game. Head coach Rilany Silva leads the U-17 National Team’s final training session before Sunday’s (01) clash against China Credits: Fábio Souza / CBF After training, forward Letícia Pinho reflected on Brazil’s World Cup campaign and highlighted the mental strength the team showed in reaching the quarter-finals. “When we talk about the World Cup, we immediately think of the challenge and have lots of questions about how it will go. But we responded really well in the first three games, managed to impose our style of play and show what Brazil is all about. In our last match, we also showed a lot of mental strength in a game that really demanded it,” she said. Speaking about Sunday’s opponents, China, Pinho stressed that Brazil will need to be mindful of the Asian team’s defensive organization and ability to exploit counterattacks. “China defend very well so they can hit you on the counterattack. So we’ve studied them very carefully to be able to counter that strength,” she explained. Confident ahead of the clash, the forward said Brazil would take an attacking approach as they look to secure a place among the world’s top four teams and keep their dream of a first-ever title alive. “The group is very well prepared, mentally and physically. Everything is in place for us to go out there and secure qualification. We’re very confident. We’ll go on the attack because we know how important this game is to stay in the competition and win our first-ever title,” Pinho concluded. item.title: Kane beat Mbappe to Ballon d'Or by just 28 points
item.description: Harry Kane beat second-placed Kylian Mbappe to the men's Ballon d'Or by just 28 points - one of the smallest winning margins in the award's history. Organisers released voting numbers on Saturday, showing that England captain Kane was awarded 1,055 points, compared with 1,027 for Real Madrid's France forward Mbappe. Bayern Munich striker Kane became the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, while France talisman Mbappe also claimed his best finish, ending up well clear of Spain forward Lamine Yamal, who was third with 881 points. It was the smallest winning margin since Argentina great Lionel Messi beat Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk by seven points in 2019, while the men's Ballon d'Or has twice been decided by a single point. That happened when England World Cup winner Bobby Charlton, who was later knighted, beat Portugal star Eusebio by the smallest possible margin in 1966, and Germany defender Matthias Sammer repeated the tight one-point victory when he edged out Brazil striker Ronaldo in 1996. Mbappe may take heart from Ronaldo's Ballon d'Or experience as the legendary frontman, who presented Kane with his award in London on Monday, went on to win in 1997 and again in 2002. Harry Kane is the fifth English player to win the Ballon d'Or, after Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966), Kevin Keegan (1978 & 1979) and Michael Owen (2001) [Getty Images] Kane clinched the prize after scoring 73 goals in 65 matches last season, helping Bayern Munich to a league and cup double and leading England to a third-place finish at the World Cup. The award is decided by votes from 100 journalists, using a weighted points system. Top 10 in the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or: Harry Kane - 1,055 points Kylian Mbappe - 1,027 points Lamine Yamal - 881 points Rodri - 726 points Lionel Messi - 612 points Khvicha Kvaratskhelia - 541 points Ousmane Dembele - 418 points Erling Haaland - 378 points Michael Olise - 296 points Fabian Ruiz - 201 points Ranking England's Ballon d'Or winners - how does Kane compare? item.title: Atletico beat Levante to move top above Barcelona
item.description: Giuliano Simeone was on target for Atletico Madrid as they beat Levante to move provisionally top of La Liga on Saturday (JOSE JORDAN) Atletico Madrid earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante on Saturday to move provisionally top of La Liga before Barcelona host Alaves later on. Diego Simeone's side climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants, who suffered their first league defeat against rivals Real Madrid last weekend. Goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone in Valencia helped Atletico record a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions. "I'm very happy with the team's work," Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar. "We're very far from the end of the season... we'll keep going game by game." There was a minute's silence at the start of the match in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Levante's Dani Requena forced Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak into an impressive early save. Morten Hjulmand thought he had put Atletico ahead after Alex Baena slipped him in, but a VAR review showed the Dane was offside. Baena, the visitors' main creative outlet, was involved in the opener. The Spaniard's pass was poorly defended by Levante and the ball bobbled through to Grimaldo, who lashed high into the net at the near post. Lee Kang-in hit the crossbar early in the second half as Atletico looked to put the game to bed. The coach's son Giuliano prodded home for Atletico's second goal after being played in by World Cup winner Baena. Oblak saved superbly from Karl Etta Eyong to stop the hosts fighting their way back into the game. It was Simeone's 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club's record set by Luis Aragones. "I don't feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years," said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011. In his absence, the offence completely dipped; the biggest indication of this was the game against the Cincinnati Bengals, when they had a 13-0 lead at halftime. In the second half, the Ravens were extremely poor not only on the offensive end, but also gave up 35 points to lose to their division rivals. However, with Jackson back, the Ravens can once again be positive about their chances to succeed; however, he has a big test in his first game back from injury. Lamar Jackson says that his ankle still hurts In just 4 games, Jackson had recorded 967 passing yards on 70.8% completion and recorded 6 touchdowns for the Ravens. In his absence, the team has only recorded a total of five touchdowns and managed to score just 53 points. Although his injury is a little bit of a concern, the quarterback is confident and is ready to deliver for the Ravens. “Yeah, I still do, but it’s bearable, that’s what I said to last week, I said ‘If it’s bearable, I’ll go out there and give it a shot, that’s what we’re doing this week,” said Jackson when asked if the pain he suffered last week was still there. The 29-year-old wanted to return for the game against the Bengals, but he was not able to, as his injury showed no sign of improvement. “I woke up [last Saturday], my ankle was swollen, so that pretty much did it,” Jackson said. “I feel like it would’ve been hard for me to make a decision on the day of the game,” said Jackson. item.description: Commanders get two kinds of awful news with Daron Payne season-ending injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . The Washington Commanders have had a rough 2026 season so far, as they're sitting at the bottom of the NFC East with a 1-4-1 record coming out of their Week 7 bye. While they have the advantage over the Philadelphia Eagles , the season is on thin ice. Terry McLaurin is out for the year, and unfortunately, the Commanders got even more bad news after a practice injury to defensive tackle Daron Payne. The star DT suffered a significant injury, and the latest update is as bad as it can get. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Commanders' DT has a season-ending injury. Payne's injury is horrible, and it's not just about the Commanders losing a key defensive player for the year. It's also a huge blow to their trade deadline plans. Commanders get two kinds of terrible news with Daron Payne update "Source: Commanders DL Daron Payne did in fact suffer a season-ending Jones fracture during Friday's practice," Schefter reports. This is a brutal blow for the Commanders' defensive lineman, and he's now going to miss a lot of time while recovering from this significant foot injury. For Jones, it comes at a bad time, as he's set to hit free agency after 2026, which means his free agency this upcoming offseason will have the season-ending injury looming over him throughout. But besides the fact that the Commanders now won't be able to rely on Payne along their questionable defensive front, the Commanders now have lost one of the most appealing trade candidates left in the NFL. To make matters worse, the compensatory pick if he leaves in free agency likely won't be strong either, as Payne might be in for a cheaper contract coming off a serious injury. This Payne injury is horrible for the player in a lot of ways, but it's also terrible for the team as well. Washington now not only has lost one of their best players, but one of their best trade assets with this brutal season-ending injury to Payne. item.title: ‘The club were considering loaning me out again, but I told them I wanted to stay and prove myself’ – Harry Kane on turning down leaving Tottenham in 2013
item.description: ‘The club were considering loaning me out again, but I told them I wanted to stay and prove myself’ – Harry Kane on turning down leaving Tottenham in 2013 Harry Kane’s (33) career has not always been plain sailing. Having come through the youth academies at Arsenal, Ridgeway Rovers FC and Watford, the Englishman eventually continued his development at Tottenham Hotspur. But before establishing himself as a legend there, the striker went through many periods of doubt. This was particularly the case during his successive loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City, where he didn’t always get much playing time. “I wondered what I could do to make the most of it: work harder on my left foot, go for extra runs after training since I wasn’t playing matches, or improve my agility with footwork drills on a speed ladder,” Kane explained in an interview with France Football . “I told myself: ‘I believe my chance will come, and I’ll be ready when it does.’ And that’s more or less what happened.” Having finally returned to Spurs in the summer of 2013, the Englishman explains that, during the transfer window, “the club were considering loaning me out again to the Championship” , but that, driven by a desire to prove himself, he refused, keen to stay and prove his worth. “I felt the time had come to take the next step. I was 20. If I didn’t manage to establish myself at that point, I was afraid I’d keep being loaned out and eventually end up being sold,” recalls Kane. “So I took a stand. I said I wanted to play and fight for my place, even though I was only the fourth-choice striker at the time.” It was a decision that paid off for the London-born player, whose fortunes changed during Tim Sherwood’s spell in charge at Tottenham. “Tim gave me my chance and I scored three goals in three Premier League matches. Of course, my journey didn’t stop there. But I knew I’d seized that opportunity,” Kane says. “I asked myself how I could use that positive momentum to keep improving.” The striker would continue to develop under Mauricio Pochettino, who made him one of the key players in his system.
